findings.problem: The opening card says 'Jesus comes down with them' but never says who 'them' is. The passage starts mid-scene (He came down with the apostles He had just chosen), and the card gives no context for who He is with or where He came down from.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: Story card has 3 sentences: 'And now the entire crowd is pressing in...' / 'It's my bakery when...' / 'Everybody's reaching at once!'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Story card has 3 sentences: 'Then Jesus looks up...' / 'His first word is "Blessed."' / 'But wait till you hear who He says it about.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Story card has 3 sentences: 'Why leap?' / 'Because great is their reward in heaven.' / 'And Jesus adds that...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Cards 9 and 11 use 'they/them/their' for the disciples ('their reward in heaven'), then the card says 'their fathers treated the prophets in the same way.' Read this way it says the disciples' fathers mistreated the prophets. In Luke 6:23 'their fathers' are the fathers of the people who hate and insult the disciples. The retelling says something the text shows is wrong.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Story card has 3 sentences: 'Then Jesus turns it around: "...comfort."' / 'Already received!' / 'That's eating the whole bowl of cookie dough...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No card tells the woe in the first half of Luke 6:25 ('Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger'). Card 12 covers 6:24 and card 13 asks only about the laughing woe, so one of the four woes, the one that mirrors the 'hunger now' blessing, is left out.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Story card has 3 sentences: 'Give to everyone who asks you...' / 'That's lending somebody your phone charger...' / 'WHEW.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke compares 'if anyone takes what is yours' (Luke 6:30) to lending someone a charger. Taking and lending are different actions. Lending also comes up as its own teaching in Luke 6:34-35, so the joke blurs the two.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Story card has 3 sentences: 'Same goes for doing good...' / 'And lending only when you expect to be paid back?' / 'Even sinners lend to sinners...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Story card has 3 sentences: 'And then the payoff.' / 'Their reward will be great...' / 'Friend, that's a better title...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Wrong answer 'rewarded' could pass as true in this passage: Luke 6:35 (and 6:23) promise that 'your reward will be great' to those who live out this teaching, so 'Forgive, and you will be rewarded' is not clearly false across the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Story card has 4 sentences: 'Then Jesus asks why...' / 'A speck.' / 'Tiny.' / 'You need glasses just to find it.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Story card has 3 sentences: 'Jesus pictures that person...' / 'I can see it now.' / 'A whole BEAM sticking out of his face...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup for this choice (the good man and the evil man bringing things out of the treasure of the heart, Luke 6:45a) appears only in the question. No story card tells it. Card 12 ends at Luke 6:44.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is always on a story card.

findings.problem: 'So He shows them...' makes Luke 6:47 a result of the question in 6:46. The text just moves on ('I will show you...') and never says how the two connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup for this choice (the one who hears and does not act, like a man who built on ground without a foundation, Luke 6:49a) appears only in the question. No story card tells it.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is always on a story card.

findings.problem: The right answer 'It fell at once and its destruction was great' sounds more like the Bible and runs longer than the plain, modern wrong answers ('It leaned hard but stayed standing', 'It was damaged and rebuilt later'), so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
